title: Stream gating bundler — memory‑sentinel batch formation for low‑jitter streaming chat
creator: Avery Zhou
description:
Problem: For streaming chat completions we observe tail jitter when many short interactive sessions interleave with long context sessions. Existing slab/microbatch strategies either underutilize GPU memory (too conservative) or cause cache thrashing (too aggressive) when KV residency spikes. Goal: design a heuristics-driven batch formation strategy — the Stream Gating Bundler — that uses a lightweight memory-sentinel signal to form micro-batches that balance latency SLOs and KV/GPU residency constraints.

Proposal summary: Introduce a memory‑sentinel subsystem that tracks per-session KV touch rate, estimated additional KV bytes on next token(s), and an EWMA GPU-residency forecast. The bundler forms two kinds of micro-bundles per GPU slab: 
- latency-lane microbundles: small, low-latency groups for sessions with high interactivity and recent-token activity;
- throughput-lane microbundles: larger aggregates for sessions with steady token rates and predictable KV footprint.

Key heuristics: 
1) Sentinel projection: maintain a per-session "sentinel" value = EWMA(estimated_kv_delta * token_prob_factor) + recent-interaction-penalty. Sessions with sentinel below a tunable threshold are eligible for aggregation into throughput-lane bundles.
2) GPU budget windows: each slab advertises a soft_residency_budget (in bytes) and a hard_residency_limit. Bundler respects soft budgets for coalescing and degrades to latency-lane when projected soft budget breaches.
3) Prefix-aware coalesce: prioritize bundling sessions that share prefix embeddings or identical model shard residency to increase KV cache locality and reduce cross-session KV warming.
4) Preemptible microbatch slots: reserve a small fraction (configurable) of slab slots for preemptible latency bursts; these slots accept high-priority sessions even if they increase per-token cost.
5) Reactive eviction hints: when sentinel forecasts predict hard_limit risk, trigger KV compaction/eviction for low-priority sessions and mark them for accelerated downstream spill to disk if available.

Acceptance criteria: 
- 95th percentile tail latency for streaming chat remains <= current SLO + 10ms under mixed workload (50% short sessions, 50% long sessions) in synthetic test harness.
- Average GPU memory residency per slab decreases by >= 12% vs current greedy coalescer in representative traces without increasing token-cost by >3%.
- No regressions on per-customer throughput SLA tests for Dedicated customers.

Rollout plan: 
1) Unit/integration tests + offline simulation run against two weeks of production traces (shadow mode) — 2 weeks.
2) Canary on 1% traffic with runtime flag; collect metrics (latency P50/P95/P99, kv_fault_rate, evictions/sec, token_cost).
3) Ramp to 10% after 48 hours if no regressions; 50% after additional 72 hours.
4) Full rollout gated by performance signal and SRE sign-off.

Metrics to monitor: p50/p95/p99 latency (streaming), avg GPU residency, kv-cache hit ratio, kv-evictions/sec, preemptible-slot-utilization, cost-per-1000-tokens.

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Over-aggressive coalescing could spike GPU residency causing OOMs. Mitigation: hard_limit fallback and circuit-breaker that disables throughput-lane on slab when eviction_rate > threshold.
- Risk: Poor prefix heuristic could accidentally group unrelated sessions. Mitigation: require a minimum prefix similarity score and cap cross-session KV sharing to same tenant or shard.

Related artifacts: design doc (internal) https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Stream+Gating+Bundler, simulation notebooks https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/stream-gating-sims, initial PR with bench harness https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2187.
